dataset.name: Classified channel masks of the East River, Colorado, U.S.A and areas of floodplain erosion and accretion ranging from 1955 to 2015
description: This dataset provides four sets of geotiffs used for the mapping and analysis an alluvial floodplain reach of the East River, downstream of Gothic, CO, U.S.A near Crested Butte. The files include binary masks of the river channel at five in intervals from 1955 to 2015. Another set of rasters provide a map of the channel centerline pixels of the river for each date. Also included in the dataset are rasters of the areas of channel change due to migration over 8 time intervals. The masks were generated from aerial and satellite imagery collected on seven dates over a sixty-year timespan: 1955, 1973, 1983, 1990, 2001, 2011, and 2015. The masks were analyzed using the Spatially Continuous Riverbank Erosion and Accretion Measurements (SCREAM) software detailed in Rowland et al. 2016 to create the channel centerlines and the change area rasters. The change masks were generated for the following time periods: 1955-1973; 1955-2015; 1973-1983; 1983-1990; 1990-2001; 2001-2011; 2001-2015; and 2011-2015.

measurementTechnique:
This dataset was derived from binary masks generated from aerial and satellite imagery acquired on seven dates over a sixty-year time period. The following summarizes the dates of the imagery, imagery source, imagery type, and acquisition platform:
Acquisition Date Imagery Source Imagery type Acquisition Platform
October 15, 1955 Army Map Service Black & White Aerial Photograph
August 4, 1973 NASA Color Infrared Aerial Photograph
September 22, 1983 NAHP Color Infrared Aerial Photograph
September 13, 1990 NAPP Color Infrared Aerial Photograph
September 21, 2001 DOQ/NAPP Black & White Aerial Photograph
August 7, 2011 NAIP Color & Near IR Aerial Photograph
September 15, 2015 World View 2 Multispectral Satellite
where NAHP is the National High Altitude Photography program, NAPP is the National Aerial Photography Program, and NAIP is the National Agricultural Imagery Program.
The binary masks of the imagery were analyzed using the Spatially Continuous Riverbank Erosion and Accretion Measurements (SCREAM) software (Rowland et al. 2016). All imagery was resampled to 1-m resolution. The 2015 imagery was orthorectified to an airborne lidar derived DEM flown contemporaneous to the imagery. All other images were georeferenced (if not already done so by the source agency) through comparison with similar point types in the 2015 georeferenced image.
Masks of the river bankfull channel location were generated using red-green-blue (RGB) color bands and the normalized difference water index (NDWI) to classify the channel water surface in each image using the object-oriented classification software, eCognition (Flanders et al. 2003). To control for variations in water levels between images, regions of tan and grey gravel and sand bars devoid of vegetation and exposed, un-vegetated bank faces were included in the channel mask as an estimate of bankfull extent. The black and white 1955 and 1973 photos were manually delineated.
Average estimated registration error for the 1-m imagery from 1973 to 2015 was 0.58 m. Poor image quality of the 1955 photographs prevented direct estimates of error using this method, so we have assigned a registration error equal to two times the highest error (1.2 m) in areas for the period between 1955-1973.
There 4 types of geotiff files in this data package.
Channel Masks: “EastRiveYear.tif”
ChannelCenterLines: “EastRiverCenterLineYear.tif”
ErodedAreas: “ERErodedAreasStartYear_EndYear.tif”
AccretedAreas: “ERAccretedAreasStartYear_EndYear.tif”
